% Figueroa RL et al. BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 2012;12:8 (PMID 22336388) = the inverse power law and its weighted fit.
Fitting the inverse power law of Figueroa et al.\ to the same-device detection curve (body rule, confidence 0.74) gives an asymptote of 81.7\% no interval lateral and 85.3\% no interval AP, reached to 95\% of asymptote by 10.0 and 12 frames; 90\% recall is not reached at any $N$ (asymptote below target in 100\% and 90\% of case-resampled fits). At the default threshold (0.25) 90\% is reached by 40 lateral and 10 AP frames and 95\% is not. 
For AP naming on the whole frame the fitted curve reaches 97\% at 68 persons no interval and 99\% at 1,071 no interval, beyond the 88 measured; with three vertebrae in view the asymptote is not identified by 88 persons (97\% at 11,584 no interval). 
Same-protocol plain films substitute for C-arm cases at 1.7 no interval per case on the whole frame but at 11 no interval with three vertebrae in view; CT renders never reach the in-domain curve.
